title: The landing wash: the orbital strike's smoke and grit thrown off the ground under the SH02's engines, from the plume's reach to a ring at the touchdown
context: The owner, 2026-11-15, with two reference images of Falcon boosters landing: "when the rocket lands, the thrusters touching the surface should create effects of smoke and particles flying ... like in the reference images of spacex boosters re-entry. perhaps we can re-use some of the nuclear strike effects after the explosion, just the smoke." Before: the arrival (src/fx/arrival.js) had its six plume sheets, a scorch decal at the touchdown and 420 tan embers for 1.2 s after it; nothing while the plume met the ground. The nuke is src/fx/explosions/orbital-strike.js on the shared kit src/fx/explosions/common.js (puff, spark and ring layers animated in the vertex shader from one clock); its base surge is puffs dragged out along the ground with a slow rise.
outcome: src/fx/landing-wash.js reuses the kit's puff and spark layers (assemble: the same template programs, cloned) as two fixed rings of slots: a puff is written into the next slot with its birth time and the shader runs it, so the wash is two draws and no allocation a frame, whatever the flight does (the flown landing can hover). src/domain/landing-wash.js: the strength (the engines' light times how far the hull has sunk into its plume's reach, full from 0.3 of it down), the ground point down the hull's axis, the emission count with its carry and a per-frame cap, the cut at the ground. The arrival feeds it every frame from the holder's own world matrix and the sheets' lit intensity, so the automatic and the flown landings (and a wreck, a bigger ring) share one path; nothing while the rocket is hidden (under the signature); it goes with the swap (settle). Knobs LANDING_WASH in src/content/story-defaults.js beside PLUME_CLUSTER: reach 1.1 of the cluster's own plume length (33 m under the feet at the 1.5 presentation scale), puffs 95 a second at full in 384 slots, a 30-puff ring at the cut (x1.6 on a wreck), grit 90 a second, a pale dust palette with the strike's fire colours for the exhaust glow in a puff's first 0.35 s. A first look cut the cloud flat along the ground (a quad half under it) and spread it to the camera: puffs now ride at 0.24-0.4 of their size over the ground as they grow, slower and shorter.
alternatives: Spawning orbital-strike bursts on a timer: rejected, each burst brings a nuclear cap and stem, and the explosions adapter keeps one nuclear burst alive at a time.
A one-shot surge at the touchdown alone: rejected, the automatic descent's last second and the flown landing's hover would show nothing while the plume meets the ground.
A new particle shader: not built, the strike's own smoke was asked for and its templates are already compiled.
evidence: test/landing-wash.mjs: the rules, then the automatic landing's clock on real three.js nodes: first puff at 28.5 m of a 33 m reach, 128 puffs and 132 grit by the touchdown, one ring of 30 at the cut and none after, still rolling 3 s on; a wreck's ring of 48.

--landing-wash (new, headless, a grown stage-1 page): first puff at t 1.47 s (28.2 m), 81 puffs and 76 grit by the touchdown, one ring, 111 puffs in all, the wash gone after the swap; stills landing-wash-low, -touch, -roll.
npm test 354 programs, npm run check, npm run architecture (td-tab unchanged at 5,365 lines).
Not measured: the frame cost in a headed browser; the flown landing's wash looked at only through the --landing suite's own stills.
